text: Row-level security restricts exactly which rows of data a user actually sees inside a semantic model — not which columns, not which workspaces, not which reports. Just rows, filtered by a role you define yourself, and it's genuinely one of the most important security concepts in all of Power BI.

Four steps, always followed in this exact order, every single time. Define the role's DAX filter expression in Desktop first. Publish that semantic model and report to the service, since the role definitions travel along with it automatically. Add specific members to that role in the service itself. And finally, validate everything with Test as role before you ever trust it with a single real user.

Here's the detail almost everyone genuinely misses the first time through: RLS only ever restricts users assigned the workspace Viewer role. Admins, Members, and Contributors all have edit access to the semantic model, so RLS simply never applies to them at all, regardless of which RLS role they might also happen to be added to.

Two more real limits worth knowing before you rely on this for anything serious. RLS filters entire rows, never individual columns — if a user can see a row at all, they see every single column of it, and restricting specific columns is a separate feature called object-level security. And belonging to more than one role at once gives you the union of both roles combined, not just the overlap between them.

One role, one DAX filter, four steps followed in order, and one crucial detail about which workspace role actually gets restricted. Lesson 80 gets fully hands-on: actually writing the real DAX filter expressions that define a role inside Desktop.
